name: Rupatadine

overview.mechanism: Antihistamine activity reduces allergic symptoms; clinical evidence below separately addresses urticaria and allergic rhinitis [[RUP-URT,RUP-PED]].
uses: Studied for chronic idiopathic urticaria in adolescents/adults and persistent allergic rhinitis using pediatric oral solution. Locally registered tablets and oral solution require their own age/formulation instructions [[RUP-URT,RUP-PED]].

evidence.title: Clinical evidence and limitations
evidence.intro: Study regimens are descriptions of research, not prescribing recommendations.

rows.design: Randomized double-blind placebo-controlled dose-ranging study; ages 12–65; four weeks.
rows.intervention: Rupatadine versus placebo for moderate/severe chronic idiopathic urticaria.
rows.findings: The two higher study regimens reduced itch severity more than placebo and improved interference with daily activities and sleep. Somnolence was more frequent in the highest study arm.
rows.limitations: Short trial; higher studied exposure is not a recommendation to exceed the local tablet label or to treat a different age group.

rows.design: Multicenter randomized double-blind placebo-controlled study; 360 children ages 6–11; six weeks.
rows.intervention: Rupatadine oral solution versus placebo for persistent allergic rhinitis.
rows.findings: Nasal symptom reduction favored rupatadine at four and six weeks; quality of life also improved. Reported adverse reactions were rare and nonserious.
rows.limitations: A pediatric solution study, not proof that tablets can be substituted or that younger children, renal impairment or dialysis were studied. The abstract symptom-score ordering is ambiguous, so numerical changes are not reproduced.

sources.citation: Once-daily rupatadine improves the symptoms of chronic idiopathic urticaria: a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled study. PubMed PMID: 17478385.
Rupatadine oral solution in children with persistent allergic rhinitis: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study. PubMed PMID: 23384091.
Health Canada: pms-RUPATADINE tablets, Pharmascience; preparation September 25, 2026. Different holder from Philippine Rupafin/Allergine; no pediatric solution equivalence implied. Link only.

draft_notes: Source-linked descriptive findings and safety information only. Current local product information, contraindications, formulation-specific dosing and renal schedules require verification.
National regulator product information is linked only; no text or numeric dose copied. Exact Philippine insert unavailable for the single-agent registrations.

common: Somnolence and headache were the most frequently reported events in the urticaria trial; somnolence increased in the highest exposure arm. “Second generation” does not mean sedation is absent [[RUP-URT]].

pediatric: Direct placebo-controlled evidence here concerns oral solution in children ages 6–11. Local oral-solution instructions must determine eligible ages and dosing [[RUP-PED]].
renal: These efficacy studies do not establish a renal dose adjustment or dialysis regimen. Product-specific renal restrictions should not be replaced by assumptions from other antihistamines [[RUP-URT,RUP-PED]].
